title: Spiral galaxy NGC 2188 and galaxy cluster Abell 3381
caption: The edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 2188 and the galaxy cluster Abell 3381, imaged by ESA’s Euclid space telescope
celestial: NGC 2188, Abell 3381 · constellation Columba · NGC 2188 about 25 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: A close-up from the first piece of Euclid’s great map of the sky, October 2024 (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Toward the middle left of this Euclid view, the spiral galaxy NGC 2188 is seen edge-on, a thin streak of stars and dust about 25 million light-years away. In the upper right, far beyond it, the galaxy cluster Abell 3381 stands out clearly at about 678 million light-years.

The picture is a cutout from a much larger mosaic that ESA released on 15 October 2024, enlarged twelve times compared with the full view. That mosaic is one early piece of the map Euclid is building, a survey of galaxies near and very far.

Two galaxies in one frame, more than 650 million light-years apart, show how much depth a single patch of sky holds. Euclid’s colors combine its visible-light camera with two near-infrared bands, and its optics give bright stars six diffraction spikes.
scale: Using the source’s listed field of view (78 × 42 arcminutes) and NGC 2188’s distance of about 25 million light-years, the frame spans roughly 570,000 × 310,000 light-years. Its light set out about 25 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Euclid combined its visible-light camera (VIS) with near-infrared measurements in the Y and H bands from its NISP instrument. Blue shows light at about 0.7 microns, green about 1.1 microns and red about 1.7 microns.
understand.eye: Two of the three colors are near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and the mapping was chosen for looks: hot stars read white-blue and dusty regions red.

explore: An edge-on galaxy shows its disc as a thin line, with dust lanes running along its length; face-on, the same galaxy would show its spiral arms.
